correctness.rationale: For each rational projective line L, binary restrictions of forms of degrees q+1 and q+2 vanishing at every point of P¹(F_q) are λ_L Δ and ℓ_L Δ, with Δ=s^q t−s t^q; geometric integrality excludes both restrictions zero. Thus every line has exactly its q+1 rational curve points and either reduced intersection or one rational doubled intersection. A degree-(q+1) projective-space rational-point equation is an alternating Frobenius minor combination. Degeneracy at a rational radical point would make its differential vanish and violate the curve Jacobian rank, forcing a nondegenerate symplectic form. Rational tangents are its isotropic lines, each of which has one unique doubled intersection; double count gives (q+1)(q²+1) tangents and a bijection. Nonrational quadratic conjugates span a rational line, contradicted by the line restriction. Adjunction gives g=1+(q+1)(q+2)(2q−1)/2 and Newton identities yield c1=q³+q²,c2=((q³+q²)²+q³+q)/2. Independent GF(2) and GF(4) point and line calculations recovered 15 rational points, 15 isotropic lines, 15 distinct tangents and no extra GF(4) points. This is a conditional all-prime-power theorem, not an assertion that the finite checker proves smoothness.
